page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The system runs on AWS ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processors operating at 2.6 GHz, providing 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of total RAM, delivering a 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio with 8.0 GB per core. For I/O-intensive workloads, the host bundles 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results reflect exceptional memory throughput and scalable multi-core processing. In Geekbench multi-core evaluation and Clang software compilation benchmarks, the system placed in the top 10 percent of servers, complemented by strong multi-core performance in stress-ng. Memory subsystems showed top-tier performance in PassMark testing, sustaining large-block uncached read speeds of 253.52 GB/s and write speeds of 116.88 GB/s. Real-world key-value tests recorded Redis SET throughput exceeding 101 million operations per second. However, single-core performance scores in Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle tier, highlighting that the instance is optimized for wide parallel execution rather than single-threaded raw speed.

The ARM Neoverse-V1 architecture provides high computational density and operational energy efficiency relative to its core count, though it requires arm64-compatible application software. The inclusion of 3.8 TB direct-attached NVMe storage minimizes latency penalties associated with network-attached block devices. Given the 512 GB memory pool, high memory bandwidth, and integrated NVMe drives, the r7gd.16xlarge is well tailored for in-memory databases, Redis key-value caching layers, real-time analytics engines, and high-concurrency database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 processors, delivering 64 dedicated physical cores at 2.6 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a generous 8.0 GB of memory per core and includes 3,800 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 30 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier memory scores, robust multi-core compiling speed, and strong Redis caching throughput of over 101 million operations per second. While single-thread processing exhibits average performance and x86 vector extensions are absent, the ARM-based hardware profile affords high computational density and efficient resource utilization for multi-threaded systems. This combination of substantial memory bandwidth, direct-attached high-speed NVMe storage, and wide core parallelism positions the r7gd.16xlarge as a solid foundation for in-memory caching platforms, real-time analytics pipelines, high-throughput key-value stores, and distributed database clusters.
